- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in recovery.
- If recent history shows sharp spikes followed by rapid decline, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- In low-sentiment environments, model often overestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 3–5% for 3–5 day horizons.
- When sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model may lag — forecast should be slightly below true value to avoid false optimism.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently negative over last 5–7 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect bearish momentum.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, consider mean reversion bias — apply downward correction of 3–7% for 10–15 day horizons.
